title: AC Impedance and Resonance Frequency

references.label: NCERT Physics Part I, Class 12 — Alternating Current

explanation: Total impedance of a series LCR circuit combines resistance with the NET reactance (inductive minus capacitive, since they act 90° out of phase with each other and with opposite sign effect). At resonance (ω = ω₀ = 1/√(LC)), XL = Xc exactly, so they cancel, leaving Z = R (minimum impedance) and hence maximum current — the working principle behind tuning circuits.

workedExample.scenario: A series LCR circuit with L = 0.5 H, C = 8 μF.

commonMistakes: Adding XL and Xc directly (like plain resistances) instead of subtracting them — they act 90° out of phase with each other, so they partially CANCEL, not add.
Forgetting impedance at resonance equals just R (minimum possible value, not zero) — current is maximum, not infinite, limited by the resistance present.
genZNote: At resonance, inductive and capacitive reactance cancel out completely — only resistance is left standing.
